points.why: It says the boundary should be set by decision type and that the 96% record is evidence only about routine tickets.
It says the agent may propose a classification but a person or rule checks it, because the agent replies in the same confident analysis-then-recommendation shape regardless.
It assigns written rules and deterministic gates to routine work, expert-checked analysis to capacity planning, and pre-written runbooks to incidents.
It describes the trust loop where good results raise trust and lower scrutiny, and proposes audits that don't depend on the track record.

pitfalls.why: It explicitly declines to grant the autonomy on the strength of the 96% figure.
